audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed with their own why-text and with the mirror. The page gave Riven levels 2, 3, first item and two items while whys[1] through whys[5] describe Illaoi owning every one of them.
audit.why: The mirror settled this chart as Riven at Level 1, Illaoi through first item, Riven at two items, and raised the rows 3 and 4 ratings to 6/10 on her side. The packet agrees on every row except Level 1, where the mirror takes precedence.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 flipped as one atomic group across both layers; Level 1 to 7/10 for Riven, the Illaoi rows to 4/10, the two-item row to 6/10. whys[0] rewritten so the Level 1 row and its reason now say the same thing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a stage to fear with no number on Leap of Faith, and the entry never mentions that Illaoi is untouchable through the slam.
audit.why: Leap of Faith is 120 seconds at rank 1 — longer than Riven's own R at that rank and by far the biggest swing timer in the lane. And per the missing-interactions data she can go untargetable through Riven's commit, which turns a full combo dumped into the animation into a wasted rotation plus a tentacle per champion hit.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rebuilt around the 120-second rank-1 cooldown and the 'do not dump the combo into the animation' rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] calls Test of Spirit 'a short E cooldown'. It is 16 seconds at rank 1 — one of the longest in the lane. The genuinely short cooldown, Harsh Lesson at 4 seconds, is never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: This inverts the whole trading rule. A player told her E is short will never wait it out, when in fact a dodged Test of Spirit buys 16 seconds. What actually beats Riven is Harsh Lesson: a 4-second dash-and-auto-reset against a 13-second Broken Wings chain, so she re-engages three times per Riven rotation. That asymmetry is the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now states 16s for Test of Spirit against 4s Harsh Lesson and 13s Broken Wings, which is the mirror's trading rule stated from Riven's side.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says Illaoi 'stacks tentacles pre-fight with W'.
audit.why: Harsh Lesson does not create tentacles. Riot's text: tentacles spawn from her passive on nearby impassable terrain (and from Test of Spirit vessels and Leap of Faith); Harsh Lesson only makes existing nearby tentacles swing at the target. Told she stacks them with W, a player watches the wrong ability and misreads the whole map — the actual tell is terrain.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] now describes her fighting beside terrain where the passive tentacles already are, then using Harsh Lesson to make them swing. whys[0] uses the same terrain rule as the Level 1 counterplay.
sources: enemyKit P text 'spawn Tentacles on nearby impassible terrain'

edits.before: Neither kit has a decisive edge at Level 1 — Illaoi hasn't stacked tentacles yet and you haven't landed W. Farm safely and track where she plants tentacles before committing anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: Illaoi has no Test of Spirit yet and tentacles only spawn on impassable terrain, so fight in open lane where Q-auto weaves beat her Tentacle Smash.

edits.before: With stacked tentacles and a short E cooldown she controls every trade window; your Q and E dashes do not let you escape a committed tentacle field — farm at range and wait for an E misfire.
edits.after: Test of Spirit is 16s at rank 1, so a dodged E is a real window — but Harsh Lesson is a 4s cooldown, and she re-engages with it faster than your 13s Broken Wings can return.

edits.before: Her Leap of Faith at Level 6 summons extra tentacles mid-fight and turns any all-in near her field into a 3v1; treat every Level 6 commit like fighting into a stacked turret and only engage in the open on a burned R.
edits.after: Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle per champion hit and she is briefly untouchable through the slam — do not dump your combo into the animation. It is 120s at rank 1, so engage in the open, after it.

edits.before: Stack tentacles pre-fight with W so she has an active field before committing
edits.after: Fight beside terrain where her tentacles live, then Harsh Lesson you so they all swing

notes: Both of the packet's suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES — Leap of Faith is the correct Riot name for Illaoi's R. The Executioner's Calling recommendation on this entry is legitimate: Prophet of an Elder God heals her whenever a tentacle damages a champion. NOT asserted: the kit file tags Leap of Faith with a 'grounding' flag ('shuts off enemy dashes'), which would be decisive against Riven's two dashes, but Riot's own description of the ability says nothing about grounding and the instructions say the description wins — so no grounding claim reached the page. If it is real it belongs in this matchup more than almost any other, and it is worth a human confirming. Left for a byte-exact pass (mojibake em dashes): tradeGood, breakdown.trading, report[3].t and breakdown.mid all refer to Illaoi as 'he'/'him', and the same strings say 'third-Q knockup' where Riot's text for Broken Wings says knock back — the mirror corrected exactly that wording from her side.
